bash.front: What is the purpose of a UNIX link?
bash.back:
**A link in UNIX is a pointer to a file.**
Like pointers in any programming language, links in UNIX are pointers pointing to a file or a directory.
Creating links is a kind of shortcut to access a file. Links allow more than one file name to refer to the same file, elsewhere.
There are two types of link, hard and soft (or symbolic).
The command is “ln”
